procedure.method: Independent fresh portfolio review of only the listed pinned inputs. Read packet/case, rules/rubric and compact method; verified all declared input hashes and byte counts. Read the five pinned native-evidence manifests before any poster view and followed none of their unlisted embedded paths. Packet source_assets and protected_layouts are empty, so there were no source image opens or protected-geometry reads. Actually opened and visually inspected all fifteen exact poster files via tools.view_image with detail original, emitted as images in this session, sequentially M1 native/usage720/thumbnail320, then M2, M3, M4 and M5 in the same three-view order. Completed all fifteen opens before the first poster copy-reading/transcription, judgment or score. First raw readings were then taken from the already opened native pixels in member and copy order, with usage/thumbnail inspection informing layout and use-size judgments; no revisit was needed. All native PNG headers independently checked as 1672x941; their aspect is not mathematically exact 16:9 but height differs from 1672*9/16=940.5 by 0.5 pixel, accepted under the pinned nearest-integer-single-edge policy. Usage files are 720x405 (width<=720) and thumbnails 320x180 (maximum edge<=320), preserving aspect to integer rounding without upsampling. No image was generated, edited, cropped or substituted. No peer review, producer inspection, planner record, resumed/forked/spawned critic or session identity was consulted or invented. This record is one critic’s judgments and does not establish the all-three-critic gate.

evidence: A single flat landscape poster uses a continuous photographic workshop scene; the open-style brief does not require tape material. No external display mockup or comparison sheet is visible.

Large people, chair, garment and tools surround the central text; this is neither a small illustration on a passive solid field nor an empty room used as a signboard. No source identity or protected geometry was supplied for comparison.
The chair, screwdriver, torn shirt and collaborating people occupy most of the frame and carry the repair message independently of the lettering.

Supporting hands and a screwdriver locate chair repair, while paired hands hold the garment around its tear; the scene expresses shared physical work.

Chair tightening and garment repair translate the specific workshop contents into a substantial scene; supporting hands make cooperation visible.
The text is placed between the two activities it describes, maintaining a direct relation between information and imagery.
Large title leads into English line, purpose, explanation, event identity and a date/time row, followed by the practical and application details.
The heading remains the principal text anchor while both repair groups still register; small logistics cease to be comfortably readable at this preview size.
Hangul, Latin letters, numerals and punctuation are clearly formed; the paragraph’s three soft lines preserve its word spacing.
The venue, fee, deadline, invitation and contiguous URL remain readable in dark type against the light table; their size is compact but adequate.
The open tabletop is a deliberate text area framed by people and objects; left-aligned text has breathing room without shrinking the activities into ornaments.
date/time row and bottom of the text column
Date and time sit on one row; lower details keep a common left edge and fit above the foreground tools without collisions.
Worn wood, shirt folds, hair and skin share coherent warm illumination; the close working poses and recognizable tools make the scene convincing.
right tear and left screwdriver contact
The garment tear and repair contact are visible, although the fine needle/screw engagement is less explicit than the larger gestures.
Concentration, close supporting gestures and warm daylight communicate a welcoming practical workshop rather than passive display.
shared table and modest worn objects
The ordinary chair and shirt keep the emotional focus on reuse and neighborly work; the finish is inviting without distracting spectacle.
No dominant extra limb, duplicated face, floating tool or contradictory perspective is evident; the foreground tools relate to the two repair tasks.
The clean text column and consistent photographic scene avoid arbitrary decorative fillers; very fine repair contact remains a minor close-inspection limit.

residuals: The lower practical copy is compact at usage720 and is not comfortably readable at thumbnail320, although thumbnail legibility of all copy is not a stated requirement.
The fine needle/screw engagement is less explicit than the strong paired working gestures; the scene is resolved professionally but not unusually refined.

evidence: whole composition in relation to M2–M5

A continuous warm photographic scene wraps people around a central tabletop text column. Its ambient depth, portrait scale and downward information route differ from the graphic hand circuit, angular detail collage, painted central figures and date-led left column.
perimeter action circuit and central logistics grid

Cropped illustrated hands, two chair views, tool handoff and red thread circulate around a broad central opening. Invitation and two-row logistics, with a top-right heading, distinguish it spatially from M1 despite both using central copy; it does not share M4’s central portrait with flanking text.
angular collage, lower-left title and pale center polygon

Photographic damaged and mended details are divided into diagonal panels, with white display words distributed across image fields and practical copy grouped in the center. This changes image editing, crop scale and reading route relative to M1’s continuous photograph and both illustrated systems.
central painted pair, foreground sewing and text on both sides

A large painted human scene and foreground garment hands divide left explanation/application from right title/logistics. This is a distinct central-figure system, even though red/blue clothing and chair repair recur in M2; its information fragmentation is a quality weakness retained separately from diversity.
red date and single left column beside right repair crop

The red serif date leads a left editorial column with brush-like Korean copy and sans-serif logistics; navy/red print-like hands and objects dominate the right. Its type roles and single-column route differ from M2’s perimeter montage despite both using hatch-textured illustration.

Both M1 and M2 reserve a center for copy, but M1 has a narrow continuous vertical column inside a real table scene while M2 uses a wide invitation/paragraph and horizontal event grid inside a circuit of isolated gestures. The distinction is greater than a material substitution.

M5 keeps event and application information in one left route; M4 splits these functions across three areas around portraits. Their viewpoints, crops and type roles differ as well as their rendering materials.
residuals: All five repeat the same two repair subjects and mostly dark type against light reading areas; this is a shared content constraint and some family resemblance, not evidence of five unique concepts by material names alone.

M1 and M2 both create central text openings, and M2/M4 share red-and-blue illustrated clothing; their whole spatial systems nevertheless differ enough for a diversity judgment of 4, rather than exceptional 5.
M4 retains scores of 3 for hierarchy and space and a literal style failure for the disconnected event/application route. Set diversity does not cancel those findings.
This independent portfolio record covers exactly the five pinned selected posters. It neither averages the seven scores nor asserts an aggregate result across the three required independent critics.
